Responsibilities

About the team
The TikTok Search team is responsible for delivering a world-class search experience across TikTok’s global ecosystem. Our mission is to connect users with the most relevant and high-quality content through advanced technologies in search ranking, recommendation, and multimodal understanding. As a campus hire, you will collaborate with top engineers and researchers to solve challenging problems at scale, working across the full stack of search—from content understanding and retrieval to ranking and user experience optimization.

Project Overview, Challenges & Value
With the rapid evolution of pre-trained large models, TikTok Search is advancing toward a new paradigm of AI-native search. Traditional search systems face increasing limitations when handling massive-scale data, multimodal content (video, text, image), and complex user intents. This project focuses on building a next-generation generative search system powered by large models to significantly enhance search intelligence and user experience.
Key focus areas include:
- Integrating large models with ranking systems to improve personalization and relevance.
- Developing end-to-end generative search models based on multimodal pretraining.
- Exploring large model–driven agent frameworks to better support complex, ambiguous, and multi-turn search scenarios.
Key challenges include:
- Personalized ranking: Fully leveraging multimodal signals beyond traditional model capacity.
- Ultra-large-scale retrieval and ranking: Scaling search systems to efficiently handle hundreds of billions of candidates.
- Complex query understanding: Accurately interpreting long, ambiguous, and multi-turn queries to improve user satisfaction.
Project Value:
- Technical Value: Drive innovation in large model–powered search architecture and enable agent-based AI search systems.
- Business Value: Significantly improve search relevance and user satisfaction, strengthening TikTok’s search engagement and long-term growth.

Your first step towards an amazing career in Research and Development (R&D) at Procter and Gamble (P&G) starts with applying to this internship. Within an R&D internship, you’ll be actively involved in creating, reimagining and launching new innovations which improve our consumers lives… all around the world.

As a company, P&G believes that ‘innovation is our lifeblood’. As such, we invest to ensure that our products best serve the current and future needs of our more than 5 billion consumers worldwide across our 65 iconic, trusted brands.

From Day 1 you’ll be equipped with cutting edge innovation tools, you’ll be encouraged to dive into the innovation process, and you’ll be tasked to advance real needs for our business. To enable your success, you’ll collaborate with talented technologists and mentors to strengthen your skillsets and develop new areas of mastery. The environments you’ll work in are creative workspaces where new ideas flourish and where your technical mastery is recognized and rewarded. Ultimately, our investment in you is equally an investment in the development of our future R&D talent and in advancing our lofty innovation goals.

What will I do?

Our Associate Scientist Interns are constantly learning, growing in service of improving how our products perform. In this role, you will find new ways to innovate, develop and manufacture consumer products. Since we’re a highly collaborative company, you will have the opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest technical and commercial partners.

We strive to match your skills, qualifications, and interests with a role that works best for you and have a number of areas in R&D where you could work as an intern, including:

- Products Research: Deeply understands our consumers and their needs in order to inform product design parameters for new or improved products.
- Product Formulation & Design: Translates the consumer’s needs into the development of delightful finished-products which use the best available technologies/chemicals/materials.

Every flight test day at REGENT generates a flood of vehicle data, and the faster that data turns into engineering answers, the faster our Seaglider programs move toward production. You'll also help build the downstream data path for our test infrastructure effort: the schemas, ingest pipelines, and quick-look analysis tools that turn raw telemetry into something engineers can actually use.

You'll sit within Mission Software Engineering, a team working across navigation and route software, perception and autonomy interfaces, vehicle deployment tooling, and the test and ground systems that support all of it. At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.

Role Overview

REGENT's mechanical team is in the middle of a defining stretch of work: carrying Squire, our production Seaglider, through a full design and release cycle, while simultaneously shaping Viceroy from early concept into preliminary design. As a Mechanical Engineering (Spring Co-Op/Summer Intern), you'll be dropped right into both efforts — designing parts in CAD, producing drawings, and supporting release on a vehicle headed toward production, while also contributing iterative design work on a program that's still taking shape. This isn't an adjacent, watch-and-learn co-op experience; you'll be trusted with real parts, real drawings, and real ownership from day one.

You'll join Hardware Engineering's Mechanical team, helping take Squire from prototype to production. The fast-moving team values sound judgment in early design and disciplined production execution. If you have a foundation in mechanical design and assembly complexity and want ownership of flight hardware bound for the water, this role could shape your education or launch a career building Seagliders that will reinvent coastal transportation.

What You'll Do

- Design and Release Squire Hardware: You'll design mechanical parts in CAD and carry them through release, stepping into a production cycle where your drawings become real hardware on REGENT's Seaglider platform. It's the kind of direct contribution that goes well beyond a typical co-op assignment.

- Help Shape Viceroy From Concept Forward: You'll jump into Viceroy while it's still being defined, doing the iterative CAD work that shapes a vehicle's geometry before anything is locked in. Bring solid engineering instincts and your early ideas will hold up, not get reworked from scratch.

- Draft With Precision: A large part of your time will go toward engineering drawings and tolerancing, turning design intent into documentation our team and manufacturing partners can actually build from. If you already have a good eye for drafting, this is where it gets put to work immediately.

- Support Manufacturing and Integration: You'll work alongside technicians during build and integration, helping fit checks go smoothly and feeding what you learn on the floor straight back into your CAD models. It's a fast feedback loop that sharpens your design judgment quickly.

- Own Systems End to End: You'll take a reasonably scoped project from concept through integration, with support from senior engineers, and build toward real ownership of at least one system on the vehicle. - CAD as Second Nature: You're comfortable living in CAD day to day, not just opening it when a class requires it. Whatever your tool of choice, you pick up new CAD environments quickly.

- An Eye for Drawings: You've spent real time with engineering drawings and tolerancing, enough to know that a good drawing is what keeps a part's design intent alive once it leaves your screen and heads to manufacturing.

- Instincts That Hold Up: You have a working sense of load paths, material choices, and how manufacturing methods shape part design. That means your early ideas are something the team can build on, not something they have to rebuild.

- Steady Under Ambiguity: You're not thrown off by incomplete information or a plan that's still taking shape. You can make a reasonable call, move forward, and adjust as new information comes in.

- A Builder's Instinct: If you've spent time in a machine shop or messing around with rapid prototyping, you know the value of walking over, testing a quick fit, and bringing what you learn straight back into the model. That loop matters a lot while Viceroy is still taking shape.

- Real Pull Toward Vehicles: You're genuinely into aerospace, marine, or vehicle programs, not just checking a box for your resume. You'll be helping shape hardware on a Seaglider headed toward production, and that should be exactly the kind of thing that gets you excited to show up.

You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.
